n6964a2db3af8: In pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), the fibroblastic stroma constitutes most of the tumor mass and is remarkably devoid of functional blood vessels, leaving unresolved how PDAC cells obtain essential metabolites and water-insoluble lipids. We find that cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) acquire and transfer lipids from blood-borne particles to PDAC cells through trogocytosis of CAF plasma membranes, a process requiring the CAF-expressed phospholipid scramblase anoctamin 6 (ANO6) to promote PDAC cell survival. Cancer cells and CAFs form synapse-like contacts that induce cytosolic calcium influx in CAFs through Orai channels, activating ANO6 and driving phosphatidylserine exposure on CAF membranes, which initiates trogocytosis and transfer of membrane lipids, including cholesterol, to PDAC cells. This ANO6-dependent phosphatidylserine externalization also supports CAF-mediated immunosuppression of cytotoxic T cells through trogocytosis. Blockade of ANO6 antagonizes tumor growth, partly by disrupting cholesterol delivery to cancer cells, and attenuates immune suppression, identifying ANO6 as a candidate therapeutic target in PDAC. Ogier et al. uncover that cancer-associated fibroblasts fuel pancreatic tumor growth and immune suppression by transferring membrane lipids to cancer cells through anoctamin 6-dependent trogocytosis.

n3398caaee053: Restless legs syndrome is a neurological disorder that disrupts sleep and quality of life, but its genetics have mostly been studied in individuals of European ancestry. Here, we perform GWAS of restless legs syndrome using data from individuals of African, Latin American, and European ancestry, followed by a multi-ancestry meta-analysis. We leverage biobank-based cohorts that established RLS diagnosis using validated clinical criteria, allowing for precise phenotypic characterization. We perform ancestry-specific association studies and post-GWAS analyses to prioritize candidate genes. Our analyses reveal ancestry differences in the genetics of restless legs syndrome. At the MEIS1 and BTBD9 loci, lead variants showed lower allele frequencies and did not reach genome-wide significance in African ancestry. We identify ancestry-specific and shared risk loci, including novel associations near GYPC/TEX51 and PRIMA1 in African ancestry and ISX in Latin American ancestry. The European meta-analysis identifies 11 additional loci and replicates 50 previously reported associations. The combined multi-ancestry analysis finds ten new loci. This multi-ancestry study broadens the genetic understanding of restless legs syndrome, and the absence or reduced frequency of key European restless legs syndrome alleles in individuals of African ancestry provides insights into known epidemiological differences. The genetics of restless legs syndrome have mostly been studied in European populations. Here, the authors perform a multi-ancestry genetic study of the condition, revealing differences in genetic risk across populations with different ancestries.
n1838fb2014c0: Recent studies have reported unprecedented accuracy predicting pathogenic variants across the genome, including in noncoding regions, using large deep-learning models trained on vast genomic data. To verify and understand the basis of these reports, we systematically evaluated the prediction accuracy of frontier models over single-nucleotide variants, focusing on general models capable of scoring multiple variant types across coding or noncoding regions. Our evaluations reveal that the performance of genome-wide predictions is severely inflated by mixing variant categories with different baseline prevalences of pathogenic variants. We constructed a benchmark stratified by variant type to identify the best-performing models for each genomic context, determine where reliable predictions remain out of reach, and establish rigorous standards to guide future evaluations. Evaluations of AI models predicting disease-causing single nucleotide variants reveal that the performance of genome-wide predictions is inflated by mixing variant types, e.g. canonical splice and 5’ UTR variants. The authors introduce a stratified benchmark to accurately identify the most robust models.

n52e5ac4db30c: Rapid Eye Movement (REM) sleep degrades with age, and more severely in Alzheimer’s disease (AD). REM sleep comprises about twenty percent of adult sleep, alternates between phasic and tonic periods, and includes delta waves (1-4 Hz) in two forms: fast sawtooth waves and slower, NREM-like waves, whose expression dynamically varies across REM periods. Yet, the functional relevance of these REM sleep delta waves remains unknown. Here, using two independent cohorts, we show that aging is associated with a shift from fast sawtooth to slow NREM-like delta waves, particularly during phasic REM sleep - a period typically marked by high cortical activation. Beyond chronological age, this shift is associated with amyloid-β and tau burden, suggesting that AD pathology is associated with REM-specific oscillatory patterns. Furthermore, this shift in REM oscillations is linked to impaired overnight memory consolidation, independent of NREM sleep quality. Moreover, variation in APOE alleles, a major genetic risk factor for AD, was independently associated with a reduction in fast sawtooth wave density, thereby linking a genetic predisposition for AD to these specific REM microstructural changes. These findings identify a signature of memory decline in aging and implicate REM sleep as a distinct vulnerable substrate through which AD pathology may impair brain function. Desel et al. report that memory loss in aging is associated with a shift from fast sawtooth to slow delta waves during REM sleep. This shift correlates with amyloid and tau burden, marking a REM sleep signature of impaired memory consolidation.

n29d22ec869eb: Inspired by organisms capable of adaptive morphological regulation, hydrogel actuators with softness and large deformability are attractive for biomedical devices and information encryption, yet remain limited by the lack of hierarchically oriented structures simultaneously enabling rapid actuation and high-order complex deformation. Here, we report a multiscale lamellar-confined assembly polymerization strategy for fabricating synchronous programmable shape-morphing and information-encoding hydrogels with hierarchically periodic lamellar-cellular structure. Owing to the periodic asymmetric stresses that amplify deformation and hierarchical porous channels that accelerate water transport, the obtained hydrogel exhibits large three-dimensional deformation with the rapidest recovery speed of 112.5°/s among the reported thermo-responsive hydrogels, facilitating programmable shape morphing by orchestrating localized curvature. Furthermore, a spatial orientation-patterning strategy is developed to precisely regulate the site-specific arrangement of lamellar-cellular structures for diverse cooperative sophisticated deformations at high speed. Importantly, the highly oriented architecture endows the hydrogel with tunable birefringence, enabling a dynamic encryption platform that couples programmable deformation with information encoding. This work provides a flexible structural strategy for preparing hydrogels with biomimetic dynamic information encryption. Hydrogel actuators have potential in a range of applications, but combining rapid actuation and complex deformation is challenging. Here, the authors report a lamellar confined assembly polymerisation strategy for preparing programmable shape-morphing and information-encoding hydrogels.

n1305839bdea3: Genetic variation can alter organ structure and function. Comparative statistical analysis of organs across genetic backgrounds requires spatial, single-cell, atlas-scale data in replicates. Here we introduce atlas-scale transcriptome localization using aggregate signatures (ATLAS), a scalable tissue mapping method that learns transcriptional signatures from single-cell RNA sequencing data, encodes them in situ with tens of thousands of oligonucleotide probes and decodes them to infer cell types and imputed transcriptomes. We validated ATLAS against direct MERFISH measurements of marker genes and through quantitative comparisons to four other technologies. We profiled 40 million cells across more than 400 coronal sections from central brains of five male and five female C57BL/6J mice and five male BTBR T+tf/J mice, an idiopathic autism model. Our analysis revealed more than 40 significant differences in cell-type distributions and identified 16 regional composition changes across male–female and B6–BTBR comparisons. ATLAS thus enables systematic comparative studies, facilitating organ-level structure–function analysis of disease models. ATLAS is a highly scalable tissue profiling method that leverages existing atlas data and in silico decoding to generate imputed cell maps.
n7b62038e9401: Providing dry solid contacts with on-demand macroscale frictional behaviour remains a formidable challenge in tribology, haptics and robotics. It has been shown that metainterfaces created from surfaces with engineered asperity-based topographies can achieve such friction control. However, only a few types of friction behaviour were demonstrated because suitable topographies were identified on the basis of human intuition. Here we introduce a numerical-optimization-based inverse design framework to automatically discover new metainterfaces that satisfy specified friction laws—relationships between friction and the normal force. To illustrate the framework’s versatility, we first expand the range of achievable friction coefficients for a given pair of materials. We next unlock friction laws showing power-law variation of frictional force with normal force, with exponents ranging between 2/3 and 1.35. We then achieve bilinear variation when the range of normal force is divided into segments, including cases for a smaller slope in the second segment than in the first. We validate relevant cases experimentally. Our automated framework enables systematic exploration of large parameter spaces, not limited to topography but potentially incorporating the individual asperities’ bulk material or surface physicochemistry. It offers design solutions for different friction laws and provides insights into the relationship between local interfacial properties and macroscopic friction. Understanding friction between contacting surfaces is important to improve device performance. Now a method is shown to discover materials that offer on-demand frictional behaviour using inverse design based on genetic algorithms.
n3e3d624f582b: Far-from-equilibrium mixtures of active and passive molecules self-organize, but the principles remain unclear. Microtubules are cytoskeletal polymers composed of 13 protofilaments bound by mixtures of actively moving motors and passively diffusing microtubule-associated proteins (MAPs). They can serve as a model system for self-organization on a multi-lane lattice. Here we show that motors can shepherd diffusive MAPs along the lattice by rectifying Brownian motion into net directional drift without motor–MAP binding. Our model reveals that biased movement increases when fewer protofilaments are accessible or when lateral diffusion between protofilaments is limited, and identifies local dimensionality and diffusion as key parameters governing spatial patterning. In particular, shepherding depends on the total number of motors bound to the microtubules, and not on the individual motor processivity. We experimentally recapitulate micrometre-scale shepherding with a kinesin-1 motor (K401) and a diffusive MAP (PRC1), which show no detectable binding. These findings suggest shepherding is an emergent mechanism by which ensembles of motors generate micrometre-scale spatial patterning and transport of MAPs without direct binding interactions. Microtubules are bound by active motors and passively diffusing proteins. Now it is shown that this mixture of active and passive molecules is a realization of rectified Brownian motion in active matter.
n7bb46a69966a: A strong potential gradient can localize individual particles in a crystal or optical lattice by making ordinary hopping energetically costly. Interactions can nevertheless enable correlated hopping processes that preserve the system’s centre of mass or, equivalently, its dipole moment. This constraint gives rise to fractonic behaviour, in which isolated excitations are immobile but their bound states can move. Here we realize individual mobile bound states of fractons in a dipole-conserving Bose–Hubbard model and observe their coherent quantum dynamics. Starting from a one-dimensional chain of ultracold bosonic atoms in an optical lattice, we use site-resolved optical potentials to deterministically generate localized dipole and antidipole excitations, which represent mobile bound states of a hole and a doublon. We track their individual quantum walks and characterize their strongly interacting scattering dynamics. Our study provides a bottom-up investigation of a Hamiltonian with kinetic constraints and offers an approach to exploring low-energy phases of fractonic matter. Strong potential gradients can localize individual particles, but interactions can still generate collective motion. An experiment with ultracold atoms in a tilted lattice now shows this collective motion by tracking mobile bound states of fractons.

n2c9c4009e46d: The candidate topological superconductor UTe2 exhibits a complex phase diagram with multiple superconducting states, and the nature of their coexistence is not yet resolved. In particular, the apparent observation of two intersecting second-order phase boundaries at a triple point in the pressure–temperature phase diagram is thermodynamically forbidden. This suggests either a hidden phase transition or a fundamental misunderstanding of the superconductivity in this material. Here we observe an additional phase boundary that is characterized by an upward jump in the sound velocity. This is direct thermodynamic evidence for a phase transition in which superconducting order is lost on cooling. Our results establish a tetracritical point beyond which the ambient and pressure-induced superconducting order parameters form a multicomponent state. We use the measured phase diagram to demonstrate that strong competition between the two superconducting order parameters drives the loss of order when cooling, and leads to phase locking that suppresses superconducting fluctuations. These findings provide the definitive magnetic field–pressure–temperature phase diagram of UTe2 and establish a thermodynamic foundation for multicomponent superconductivity. Prior measurements of the phase diagram of UTe2 contain a triple point that is forbidden by thermodynamics. Now, an additional phase boundary is discovered that resolves this problem and confirms multicomponent superconductivity in this material.

nc6f97e83e90f: Despite decades of investigation, the fundamental molecular and cellular principles that enable bacteria to thrive within the tumor microenvironment have yet to be defined. Here, through a genome‑wide functional screen, we identify the bacterial genes and pathways that govern intratumoral fitness. Targeted deletion of nonglucose phosphotransferase systems to align bacterial metabolic preference with tumor metabolite availability promotes bacterial intratumoral fitness. Integrating multiple metabolic adaptations into a single tumor‑avid Escherichia coli strain (Ec‑TA) results in increased tumor colonization, not only after intratumoral delivery but also after intravenous delivery, leading to increased anti‑tumor efficacy when using Ec‑TA engineered to deliver an encoded immunostimulatory payload. Furthermore, Ec‑TA displaces wild‑type bacteria from pre‑colonized tumors when administered systemically, underscoring its potential for locally delivering therapeutics in the presence of resident tumor microbes. These data demonstrate that adapting bacteria to the unique characteristics of the tumor metabolic microenvironment can drive the development of safer and more effective chassis for next‑generation bacterial cancer therapies.

n25d2c88ba945: Immune-related adverse events (irAEs) affect up to 40% of patients receiving immune checkpoint inhibitors, yet identification requires laborious, inconsistent manual chart review. Here we show that agentic artificial intelligence coupled with human verification could enhance efficiency, performance and consistency for irAE assessment. We developed and evaluated an agentic large language model system to extract the presence, temporality, severity grade, attribution and certainty of six irAE types from clinical notes. Retrospectively, the system achieved a macro-averaged F 1 of 0.92 for current-event detection and 0.66 for multi-class severity grading; self-consistency improved F 1 by 0.14. The best-performing configuration cost approximately US$0.02 per note. In prospective silent deployment over 3 months, the binary F 1 was 0.72–0.79. In a randomized crossover study of clinical trial staff, agentic assistance reduced annotation time by 2.71 min ( P < 0.001), increased complete-match accuracy (odds ratio 1.45; 95% confidence interval 1.01–2.08; P = 0.045) and improved interannotator agreement (Krippendorff’s α from 0.22–0.51 to 0.82–0.85).

n1c0537527e38: Atom transfer radical reactions-encompassing atom transfer radical addition (ATRA)1 and atom transfer radical polymerization (ATRP)2-provide a versatile route to synthesize functionalized small molecules and polymers. Using readily available unactivated alkyl chlorides3 instead of activated organohalides represents the state-of-the-art in this field, as this requires cleaving stronger C-Cl bonds in the substrates while preserving weaker ones in the products. Here we describe a dual-copper relay catalytic strategy to overcome this limitation. A dinuclear copper complex selectively activates the robust C-Cl bond of unactivated alkyl chlorides, while a mononuclear copper catalyst mediates controllable C-Cl bond reconstruction. The reaction pathway can be switched between ATRA and ATRP-type reactions in the presence or absence of the mononuclear copper partner, thus providing a switchable platform for chlorine atom transfer radical reactions. This protocol can not only enable synthesis of structurally diverse ATRA products and α-end-functionalized polyacrylates, but allow for direct modification of poly(vinyl chloride) (PVC) under mild reaction conditions. It demonstrates the successful utility of unactivated organochlorides in organic synthesis and polymer science.

n022b6e8e0f3e: Highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) clade 2.3.4.4b H5N1 virus has recently emerged in dairy cattle in the USA, leading to mastitis and sharp reductions in milk production. Eight cows were divided into vaccinated and control groups, receiving two intramuscular doses of the vaccine or saline, followed by intramammary viral challenge. Vaccination elicited HA-reactive and neutralizing antibodies in serum and HA-reactive antibodies in milk. Following viral challenge, vaccinated cows had ~1,000-fold lower peak viral RNA in milk and a lower occurrence of mastitis and mammary fibrosis. Dairy cows are protected from H5N1 influenza by an mRNA vaccine.

n385ecb46a983: Past outbreaks of zoonotic viral infections highlight the importance of understanding respiratory virome ecology. As major food-producing animals with frequent human contact, cattle represent a critical host at the human-animal interface; however, the early-life establishment of their respiratory virome and its evolutionary connections to viruses from other hosts remain underexplored. Here, we longitudinally profile the upper respiratory tract (URT) virome of beef calves from birth to weaning using an optimized viral enrichment procedure and metagenomic workflow. Viral communities exhibited increased richness and turnover, reflecting ecological structuring during early life. Temperate phages dominate the URT phage community and share virulence- and mobility-associated genes with bacterial hosts, likely contributing to host adaptation and colonization persistence. Vertebrate-associated viruses emerge after the first week of life. Targeted reassembly from bovine URT viromes recovers near-complete betacoronavirus-like (CoV-D180) and adenovirus-like (AdV-D56) genomes positioned phylogenetically between bovine and human viral lineages. Competitive mapping of bovine-derived CoV-D180 and AdV-D56 to human respiratory metatranscriptomic datasets reveals genome-specific, regionally structured coverage patterns distinct from reference viruses, supporting shared sequence features in conserved genomic regions across host-associated viral lineages. Collectively, these findings reveal early-life assembly dynamics of the bovine respiratory virome and highlight cross-host signatures in a One Health framework. In this study, the authors use longitudinal metagenomics profiling to show that cattle upper respiratory viromes display age-dependent succession and phage-linked bacterial adaptation during early life, and harbor bovine-derived coronavirus and adenovirus genomes reflecting cross-host evolutionary signatures.
nc63271e9a13c: The Great Oxidation Event about 2.4 billion years ago transformed Earth’s atmosphere and forced early life to adapt. This study shows that proteins across the tree of life became progressively more oxidized over this period, consistent with evolution favouring lower-energy sequences.
n06924fc34d52: The stoichiometry of particulate organic matter (POM) in the ocean influences global elemental cycles, but elemental distributions within macromolecule classes that comprise POM (e.g. lipids) are poorly constrained. Using publicly available datasets of lipids, nutrients, and POM stoichiometry, we conduct a basin-scale survey of lipid stoichiometry spanning the western Atlantic Ocean from ~40°S to ~55°N, and demonstrate that surface ocean lipid stoichiometry variability is primarily linked to phosphate availability and is strongly correlated with POM stoichiometry. We evaluate lipid biomarkers of nutrient scarcity, finding they are not uniformly in agreement. We then describe a lipid class, diacylglycerylcarboxyhydroxysulfocholine, only known in the coccolithophore genus Gephyrocapsa, potentially indicative of nitrogen and phosphorus stress. We advance three biomarkers of nutrient scarcity, specific to oligotrophic heterotrophic bacteria and to the coccolithophore, G. (ex Emiliania) huxleyi, and elucidate a transition from nitrogen to phosphorus stress in the Atlantic Ocean. In the surface Atlantic Ocean, microbial lipid stoichiometry is highly variable and is linked to phosphate availability. Lipid biomarkers can be used to determine where different microbial clades are experiencing resource scarcity.

n023325cfd732: Extending the depth reach of multiphoton microscopy for imaging neuronal population activity in the scattering mammalian brain is an ‘exponentially hard’ problem. Three-photon (3p) microscopy has enabled imaging of neuroactivity at depths up to ~1.2 mm in the mouse brain; however, the fundamental depth limit of 3p imaging, as set by the depth at which out-of-focus background fluorescence exceeds the in-focus fluorescence signal, is well beyond 2 mm. Reaching this fundamental depth limit in 3p imaging has been hampered by insufficient in-focus fluorescence signal. Here we demonstrate a three-photon ultra-deep imaging (TrUDI) system that approaches this fundamental depth limit via systematic and principled optimization of the in-focus fluorescence signal. TrUDI matches the parameters of the excitation laser, the optical system, and the acquisition to linear and nonlinear limits for safe laser exposure while satisfying the spatiotemporal requirements of single-cell resolution calcium (Ca2+) imaging. TrUDI achieves a ~250-fold increase in detected fluorescence photon yield at the same laser power as in previous approaches thereby enabling in vivo cellular-resolution recordings of neuronal population activity within fields of view of ~230 × 230 µm2 at 8.6 Hz at tissue depths of up to ~2 mm in mouse cortex and hippocampus. TrUDI is an optimized three-photon imaging approach that allows structural and functional imaging of neuroactivity up to a depth of 2 mm in the mouse brain.

n75eeaa4d85d6: Cytotoxic CD8+ T cells induce target-cell death by producing effector proteases called granzymes. Most granzymes, as exemplified by granzyme B, induce apoptosis by cleaving intracellular substrates after delivery to target cells via the immunological synapse. By contrast, it was recently shown that granzyme K (GZMK), which is selectively expressed by a unique population of CD8+ T cells, activates the complement cascade instead of executing direct cytotoxicity. In this Perspective, we summarize recent data on complement activation by CD8+ T cell-derived GZMK that points to a novel lymphocyte-mediated pathway of complement activation. We present evidence that GZMK-expressing CD8+ T cells have distinct pro-inflammatory effects in tissues and discuss their involvement in an array of chronic and inflammatory diseases. Furthermore, we propose the concept of 'tissue histotoxicity' as a core feature of GZMK-expressing CD8+ T cells. We suggest this as a defence strategy that enables the immune system to act on a tissue neighbourhood instead of targeting one cell at a time. Finally, we discuss the possibility of GZMK expression being a heritable trait in subsets of memory T cells.
n0d02d0a10b8f: The SARS-CoV-2 spike protein binds its receptor ACE2 to initiate target-cell infection. To engage ACE2, at least one of the three receptor-binding domains (RBDs) of the spike must adopt the up orientation. Here, we describe S22, a potent, bioavailable, and non-toxic inhibitor of BA.2 and all subsequent Omicron variants. Cryo-EM analyses showed that S22 assembled as a trimer in the central cavity of the spike apex, stabilizing all three RBDs in the down orientation, thereby preventing ACE2 association. Binding studies, especially those using mixed S22-sensitive and -resistant spikes, imply a cooperative assembly of three S22 molecules with three RBDs, resulting in an unusually slow S22 off-rate. Consistent with its slow dissociation and favorable pharmacokinetics, S22 suppressed viral replication and inflammation in the lungs of XBB.1.5-infected female mice. Thus, S22 potently inhibits Omicron entry through a distinct mechanism whereby a small compound assembles cooperatively as a trimer to stabilize spike in an inactive conformation. In this study, the authors identify S22 as a potent inhibitor of SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variants and use structural analysis to show that it prevents infection by assembling as a trimer into a trimeric spike protein cavity, locking the spike in a closed, inactive state.

n901edc1d018f: Tissue-resident macrophages originate from distinct developmental sources, but their adult replenishment is thought to depend exclusively on circulating monocytes. Here we identify a previously unrecognized CD4-lineage erythro–myeloid progenitor (EMPROR) in the adult bone marrow that provides an alternative pathway for macrophage generation. EMPROR cells are phenotypically and transcriptionally distinct from hematopoietic stem cells, common myeloid progenitors and monocyte precursors, lacking Csf1r and Ccr2 while expressing Cd4 and Kit . Single-cell RNA sequencing, RNA velocity analysis and lineage assays reveal macrophage, neutrophil, megakaryocytic and erythroid potential. EMPROR cells generate perivascular and tumor-associated macrophages independently of CCR2-mediated monocyte recruitment and contribute to erythroid and granulocytic lineages under inflammatory and neoplastic conditions. Transcriptomic comparisons position EMPROR cells closest to embryonic erythro–myeloid progenitors, indicating the persistence of an embryonic-like program in adult bone marrow. These findings reveal an alternative pathway of adult myelopoiesis that sustains macrophage diversity beyond the classical monocyte lineage.
nae3a28f57f56: Two studies shed new light on macrophage origins. Perivascular macrophages derive from extraembryonic erythromyeloid progenitors arising at a newly discovered hematopoietic site at the maternal–fetal interface and a related population of adult bone marrow progenitors.
n38ac05f045de: Embryonic hematopoiesis is thought to occur exclusively in the extraembryonic yolk sac before hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) arise in the aorta–gonad–mesonephros region. Here we identify a previously unrecognized hematopoietic site at the maternal–fetal interface in mice, termed MIXER (Maternally Interfaced eXtraEmbRyonic) tissue, which develops contemporaneously with the yolk sac and exhibits robust hematopoietic activity. MIXER contains abundant hematopoietic precursors, including classical CSF1R + erythro-myeloid progenitors and a unique embryonic CD4 + CSF1R − Erythro-Myeloid PRogenitOR (eEMPROR) population. Lineage-tracing experiments demonstrate that eEMPROR cells contribute to select macrophage subpopulations during fetal development, primarily in the perivascular space. Notably, early human placental villi, before HSC emergence, also harbor CD4 + nucleated erythrocytes, indicating a conserved hematopoietic role for the maternal–fetal interface. These findings establish MIXER as an anatomically distinct niche for embryonic hematopoiesis and expand the developmental map of blood cell emergence in mammals.

n04b38b8fc204: In patients with non-Hodgkin lymphoma (NHL) treated with chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell therapy, factors associated with efficacy overlap with prognostic biomarkers. Currently, there is no consensus on optimal product characteristics. We analyzed the phenotypic attributes of the anti-CD19 CAR T therapy axicabtagene ciloleucel (axi-cel) from 580 patients with NHL across multiple clinical trials with long-term follow-up (median, 41.9 months). A high proportion of naive-like (CCR7+CD45RA+) T cells was the most significant feature associated with prolonged progression-free survival (PFS; hazard ratio = 0.46, 95% confidence interval: 0.31−0.68, P = 9.8 × 10−5, high versus low naive-like T cell groups) without impacting safety. The relationship between naive-like T cells and efficacy was independent of tumor microenvironment characteristics (assessed in 112 patients). In multivariate models, the naive-like phenotype outperformed clinicopathologic features such as inflammatory markers and tumor burden, remaining significant after adjusting for product expansion. An inverse correlation was observed between prior lines of therapy and the proportion of naive-like T cells in both product and matched apheresis samples, suggesting a benefit of earlier intervention. The key findings were validated in an independent cohort of 203 patients treated with axi-cel-based therapy or brexucabtagene autoleucel. Mass cytometry by time-of-flight analysis of products from a subgroup of 116 patients confirmed an association between a CD8 naive-like T cell phenotype lacking expression of exhaustion markers, such as TIGIT, LAG-3 and PD-1, and PFS. A large comprehensive analysis of clinical trial samples from patients with non-Hodgkin lymphoma who were treated with anti-CD19 CAR T therapy shows that a high proportion of naive-like and stem cell memory-like CCR7+CD45RA+ T cells in the pre-infusion CAR T product correlates with improved and prolonged clinical benefit, which was validated in an independent external cohort including different products.

nf7d4cc848f72: Here we present DynaVelo, a generative neural ordinary differential equation model that learns the joint dynamics of gene expression and transcription factor (TF) motif activity from single-cell multiome data. n5b8538ecaa59: Transcriptomic measurement technologies provide powerful approaches to understand biology but are limited to providing either a high-resolution snapshot at a moment in time or a low-resolution history of transcription constrained to a few genes over a narrow time range. Here, we introduce the ‘recordanelle’, a single-component synthetic organelle capable of recording the transcriptome in human cells. Recordanelles are composed of a mitochondrial membrane anchor, a condensate assembler and a poly(A)-binding protein. We demonstrate that the recordanelle can be engineered to recruit engineered RNAs or a sampling of up to 90% of all endogenous mRNAs and protect them over several days. n47dd3958d0c0: The breakdown of Hooke’s law marks the onset of nonlinear behaviour: when displacements become large, restoring forces weaken and Hookean proportionality fails. nf4002d7207e2: In conventional, phonon-mediated superconductors, the transition temperature and the linear-in-temperature normal-state scattering rate are linked through the electron–phonon coupling strength. n2c7b769c5806: Thermodynamics establishes that information acquired through measurement can be converted into work, as exemplified by Maxwell’s demon and Szilard engines. Most experimental realizations of information engines, however, implicitly assume Markovian environments, in which information exchanged with the surroundings is irreversibly lost. Many physical systems instead exhibit environmental memory, with hidden degrees of freedom retaining correlations with the history of the system and giving rise to non-Markovian dynamics. Whether and how such concealed memory can be harnessed as a thermodynamic resource has remained an open question. Here we experimentally demonstrate the extraction of work from environmental memory. Using time-resolved measurements on an optically trapped Brownian particle in equilibrium, we implement a time-delayed double-measurement protocol that retrieves information through backflow from hidden bath degrees of freedom. We show that this information backflow alters the relaxation dynamics, can be quantified independently of initial state effects and—when appropriately exploited—enhances work extraction. Notably, we identify regimes in which the extracted work exceeds the energy stored in the observable degree of freedom alone. Our results establish environmental memory as an experimentally accessible thermodynamic resource and reveal how non-Markovian dynamics can be systematically explored to improve the performance of information engines operating in time-correlated environments.

n6ab0eab91600: Changes in oscillatory neural dynamics reflect—but may not necessarily determine—transitions between sleep stages and variations in sleep pressure. nab98ef4391a8: Silicon spin qubits offer a promising path to scalable quantum computing due to their compatibility with industrial semiconductor manufacturing. n538ada7aaa44: Planets are inherently three-dimensional objects shaped by their thermal structure and dynamics. We are also able to constrain the abundances of H 2 O and CO 2 to constant values around the limb, providing observational constraints for results from global circulation models. ne244b80c0746: The rapidly growing census of exoplanets now includes over a thousand multi-planet systems, revealing architectures that span more than four orders of magnitude in mass and five in orbital scale. n01b97ded6e89: Cancer cachexia is a wasting syndrome with outsized impact on morbidity and mortality, yet its drivers and systemic consequences remain poorly defined. In this study, we repurposed longitudinal clinicogenomic data from 52,236 patients with cancer profiled by MSK-IMPACT (2010–2024) at Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center to define episode-resolved trajectories of consensus-defined cachectic weight loss and linked these events to outcomes, serology and tumor genotypes. Cachectic episodes clustered near periods of disease progression and were associated with inferior outcomes in nearly all cancer types. Across diverse malignancies, cachectic weight loss episodes exhibited a consistent serologic signature characterized by lower albumin and hemoglobin and higher levels of liver enzymes. Numerous somatic tumor genotypes, including TP53 mutation across several diseases, were also associated with more frequent onset of cachectic episodes. Motivated by these observations, we developed a multivariate model to predict impending risk of cachectic weight loss in patients with lung, colorectal and prostate cancer, validated in an independent, external cohort from Dana-Farber Cancer Institute (n = 5,785). Routine clinicogenomic data are, therefore, a scalable resource for discovery in cancer cachexia. Using longitudinal data from 52,236 patients with cancer, this study created a multimodal atlas of cancer cachexia, demonstrating that weight loss episodes are linked to systemic serologic signatures and specific tumor genotypes and can be predicted using integrated clinical and molecular data, enabling earlier identification.

n23b287ead930: Clinical prediction models are increasingly deployed to support diagnostic and prognostic decisions, making reproducibility essential for assessing their reliability and generalizability. Analytical code supports independent assessment of these processes, yet its availability in the literature remains limited. This scoping review quantifies current practices in sharing analytical code to inform the development of TRIPOD-Code, a reporting guideline for code availability and reproducibility. Here a large-language-model-assisted pipeline was developed to screen articles citing TRIPOD or TRIPOD+AI, extract repository links and assess retrieved repositories against 14 predefined reproducibility-related features. Among 3,967 articles, 482 (12.2%) included code-sharing statements. Sharing prevalence varied widely by journal and country. Repository assessment showed substantial heterogeneity in reproducibility features. These findings underscore the need for clearer expectations beyond code availability, including documentation, dependency specification and executable structure. Strengthening these practices may improve the usability of clinical prediction model studies and support their deployment in real-world clinical settings. An analysis of code availability in the open-access published literature shows that code sharing in clinical prediction models remains limited and reveals significant variability in practices and documentation quality.

n4dd3906d7305: Programmable quantum devices provide a platform for controlling the coherent dynamics of quantum wave functions. Monitoring and feedback can control classically chaotic dynamics, but extending these approaches to quantum systems is challenging because chaotic evolution amplifies perturbations and is sensitive to noise and decoherence. Here we demonstrate adaptive monitored quantum circuits that incorporate conditional feedback into non-unitary evolution, using local mid-circuit measurements and resets to control quantum chaotic dynamics. We perform the experiments on an IBM superconducting quantum processor with up to 100 qubits, implementing a quantum version of the classically chaotic Bernoulli map. The map scrambles quantum information, whereas local measurements and feedback attempt to steer the dynamics towards a fixed point of the map. This competition drives a dynamical phase transition between quantum and classical dynamics, which we observe experimentally and describe theoretically using noisy simulations, matrix product states and mappings to statistical mechanics models. By successfully applying up to nearly 5,000 entangling gates and 5,000 non-unitary mid-circuit operations on systems up to 100 qubits, the quantum processor yields accurate estimates of the universal critical properties. Controlling quantum chaos requires using measurement and feedback that survive noise and decoherence. Such control is now achieved in a superconducting quantum processor and reveals a critical transition between quantum and classical dynamics.

n8578cfe7cc73: The Sun continuously releases a stream of charged particles known as the solar wind, threaded by magnetic field lines that occasionally fold back on themselves in sharp reversals called magnetic switchbacks. These structures are frequently observed by spacecraft near the Sun, but their formation mechanism remains an open question. Using measurements from Solar Orbiter at 0.55 AU, we report heavy ion observations within a magnetic switchback that provide direct evidence of its solar source. Elevated charge-state ratios of oxygen and carbon, combined with a depletion of helium relative to protons, indicate that the switchback plasma originated from hot, closed coronal loop structures. A semi-empirical coronal model, constrained by electron temperature and density measurements from the Solar Dynamics Observatory, traces the ion signatures to either a coronal hole boundary or loops within the coronal hole, implicating the source mechanism as interchange reconnection, where closed loops reconnect with open magnetic field and eject plasma. The proton velocity and magnetic field fluctuations of the switchback are in accordance with an outward-propagating Alfvén wave. These findings suggest that interchange reconnection and wave or turbulence mechanisms jointly govern switchback origin and propagation, respectively. Most importantly, we show that switchbacks preserve measurable signatures, carrying information about the physical processes that heat the solar atmosphere and accelerate the solar wind.

n37c02bf0e6b1: Excitons—bound states of electrons and holes—can spontaneously condense into a quantum coherent ground state. 1 T -TiSe 2 , a layered transition metal dichalcogenide, is a candidate for realizing this phase in a bulk material, but its putative excitonic condensation is accompanied by charge-density-wave formation that obscures signatures of excitonic instability and fluctuations in this structural transition. n1fb12d5b6ff8: Many white dwarfs accrete the debris of disrupted planetary bodies, detected in the form of metal enrichment in their atmospheres, dusty or gaseous circumstellar discs, and photometric transits from debris. The composition of accreted debris has been shown to be diverse yet overall closely resembles Solar System bodies. Here we report the discovery of a white dwarf accreting material that is unlike any Solar System object. The atmosphere of HS 0209+0832 is strongly enriched in trans-iron elements including zinc, copper and niobium but depleted in the canonical rock-forming elements silicon and iron. The composition of the accreted object is consistent with a candidate second-generation planet, formed from the stellar material ejected during the giant phase. The key abundance signature that differentiates it from a first-generation planet is the high enrichment of s-process elements. Photospheric helium and the absence of terrestrial rock-forming elements implies that the white dwarf is accreting from the escaped atmosphere of a photo-evaporating giant planet candidate. This is further supported by the detection of a sinusoidal photometric period of 4.399 ± 0.026 days at an amplitude of 0.120% ± 0.018%, which we attribute to thermal emission phase variability from a planetary day–night cycle or a transiting cometary tail of an evaporating gas giant. The discovery of this second-generation planet that is chemically distinct from first-generation material demonstrates that close-in planets around white dwarfs can form after the main sequence.

nc74c55b8ddc8: Liquid chromatography is a predominant technology for the separation of small molecules. Hundreds of retention time prediction models have been published over the past decades, yet truly transferable prediction (requiring no training data from the target chromatographic system) remains an open challenge. Unfortunately, retention times may change massively, even for nominally identical chromatographic conditions. Retention order is considerably more conserved; but even retention order may change if chromatographic conditions vary. Here we present 2-step, a two-step method for the prediction of retention times in reversed-phase chromatography. In the first step, a machine-learning model predicts a retention order index, taking into account chromatographic conditions. In the second step, we map predicted indices to absolute retention times. Disentangling these two tasks finally enables transferable retention time prediction across chromatographic conditions and compound classes, without requiring any target-system training data. Our 2-step method outperforms existing methods that were trained on the target dataset. Finally, we systematically study what chromatographic conditions result in notable changes of retention order. A method for transferable retention time prediction across chromatographic conditions and compound classes is presented. The approach makes use of a two-step strategy that first predicts a condition-aware retention order index followed by mapping it to absolute retention times.
naa76afd8a6b6: There are no currently approved therapies that promote new myelin formation after myelin damage, which can, in part, be attributed to a lack of reliable systems that can reproducibly model these processes. Here we engineered a human iPSC-derived spheroid model enriched with mature, myelinating oligodendrocytes and functionally reactive microglia. This model enables the study of human central nervous system remyelination after a demyelinating insult by recapitulating processes of myelin damage and repair. These include myelin fragmentation, microglial reactivity and phagocytosis of myelin debris, oligodendrocyte generation and differentiation, and axonal ensheathment with newly formed myelin. We show that newly generated oligodendrocytes contribute to remyelination, and use ultrastructural quantification to demonstrate that remyelinated axons are ensheathed by thinner myelin after injury. Altogether, we provide a model to interrogate otherwise inaccessible aspects of human myelin biology relevant to multiple sclerosis, providing mechanistic insights into disease pathways and a platform for drug screening.
n524dbae5bfc0: Aging and Alzheimer’s disease (AD) are accompanied by alterations to large-scale communication patterns in the brain, which can be tracked in vivo using functional connectivity. The location, direction and relevance of these changes remain widely debated, although they are rarely studied in the context of whole-cortex communication dynamics. Here, in two independent cohorts (BioFINDER-2, N = 973; Alzheimer’s Disease Neuroimaging Initiative, N = 129), we show that functional connectivity changes associated with aging and AD are strongly aligned with separate fundamental axes of hierarchical brain communication. Early accumulation of AD pathology and subsequent cognitive decline are both linked to functional change along the sensory–association axis. Meanwhile, age-related functional changes occur along the representation–executive axis consistently throughout the adult lifespan. These findings together suggest that both AD and aging alter major but orthogonal functional pathways in the brain. More broadly, our findings position whole-brain connectivity dynamics as a unifying framework for interpreting functional changes across the adult lifespan.

n5acdbdbab64a: Below every step we take there is groundwater. Out-competing rivers, lakes and wetlands in terms of water quantity and quality, shallow aquifers are an essential reservoir of freshwater for the human population. At the same time, they represent the largest freshwater biome on earth, forming a responsive but vulnerable interface between the highly dynamic surface aquatic and terrestrial ecosystems and the environmentally static deeper zones of the subsurface. Shallow aquifers are home to a vast phylogenetic and functional microbial diversity, regularly surpassing those of surface environments. Predominantly colonized by microorganisms, key drivers of community composition and biogeochemical cycles are the hydrogeological settings, availability of energy and prevailing redox conditions, as well as climate and local to regional anthropogenic activities. Although there is steadily growing knowledge on microbial biodiversity and their potential functions, quantitative data on active key processes, such as carbon cycling, are scarce. We do have a very incomplete idea of the abundances and distribution of viruses, protists and fungi and their ecological role in groundwater. In this Review, we discuss current and future pressures to shallow groundwater ecosystems in terms of microbial community dynamics particularly in light of global and climate change, that is, groundwater pollution and warming. In this Review, Karwautz and Griebler examine the microbial communities found in shallow groundwater and aquifers, exploring their diversity, functional roles and dynamic interactions with adjacent terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems, as well as the influence of global change and anthropogenic pressures on these microorganisms.
n4b9ffc1314b2: Microorganisms facilitate both the synthesis and breakdown of bio-based biodegradable plastics, which positions them as central players in the development of a future circular plastics economy. However, advances in microbial production and biodegradation of plastics are often considered in isolation, limiting our ability to integrate these processes into viable circular systems. In this Review, we discuss the contributions of microorganisms across the life cycle of key bio-based polymers, focusing on polyhydroxyalkanoates, bacterial nanocellulose, and the monomers of polylactic acid and polyethylene furanoate, and we critically assess the extent to which current microbial capabilities can support polymer synthesis and degradation. Although the genetic capacity for these processes is widespread, this does not necessarily translate into efficient synthesis or biodegradation in industrial or environmental conditions. Microbial synthesis remains constrained by low volumetric productivity, carbon inefficiencies and downstream processing challenges, whereas biodegradation is highly dependent on material properties and environmental conditions, with efficient biodegradation often limited to managed settings. Thus, achieving an effective circular bio-based plastic economy requires the integration of microbial engineering, polymer chemistry, material science and other disciplines to optimize both production and end-of-life management. In this Review, O’Connor and colleagues discuss the contributions of microorganisms across the life cycle of key bio-based polymers and assess the current role, the potential and limitations of microbial production and degradation of bio-based polymers as well as the implications for integration of microbiological processes into a circular bioeconomy.
